ceiling: AUDIT_ONLY. Documents a rights-clean data-source search and files acquisition-queue asks + proposed_followups; does not acquire, cache, or ingest any external dataset, does not modify the AD gate or any shipped KPI, and does not modify the manifest.

claim_under_attack.claim_text: Rights-clean training corpora exist that would widen the applicability domain to cover industrially relevant epoxy-amine chemistry.

objective: Domain-widening data hunt: search for rights-clean (CC-BY / CC0 / public-domain / explicit permissive) corpora with measured or simulated Tg / density / refractive index / dielectric for amine-cured epoxy systems or their constituent monomers, reporting for each candidate: source+DOI, licence quoted verbatim, record count, property coverage, structural overlap with the 5 canonical amines + grammar-38, and the concrete next action.

proposed_followups.defect: AD gate (coating-candidate-design-card-5-canonical-epoxy-amines-kpi.v1.json) excludes DETA (one of the 5 canonical amines) despite a rights-clean CC-BY-4.0 Mendeley dataset (10.17632/bypjxzm3fn.1) containing a DETA-cured DGEBA system with measured Tg -- this row is not yet acquired/ingested.
proposed_followups.proposed_done_criterion: A future fire acquires the Mendeley Data CSV under its CC-BY-4.0 license, hand-verifies >=1 Tg row for the Epikure-3223(DETA)/Epon-828(DGEBA) system against the published article, adds it to the training corpus with full provenance, and re-runs the U-AD sweep to show DETA's AD-admission status after the addition.

proposed_followups.defect: grammar-38 novel hardener candidate 'MDA/DDM(methylene)' has zero training-corpus representation despite a rights-clean CC-BY-4.0 Zenodo record (doi 10.31142/ijtsrd15748) reporting a DDM-cured epoxy composite -- exact structural match (Tanimoto=1.0), full-text not yet read.
proposed_followups.proposed_done_criterion: A future fire reads the CC-BY-4.0 full text, extracts the reported property table for the DDM-cured GELR-128 system, and files it as a rights-cleared candidate training row with a data-ask receipt naming the exact table/page cited.

proposed_followups.defect: NIST ThermoML/TRC holdings were assumed public-domain by a prior informal reading of general NIST copyright policy; this fire found that TRC/ThermoML data is explicitly Standard Reference Data (SRD), a carved-out exception under 15 U.S.C. 290e, and the archive's own page states files are available 'with permission of the journal publishers' -- i.e. NOT a blanket rights-clean grant.
proposed_followups.proposed_done_criterion: A future rights-review fire enumerates which specific ThermoML journal-cooperation agreements (if any) grant redistribution/derivative-training rights beyond read-access, or formally closes this as BLOCKED_RIGHTS if none do.

proposed_followups.defect: PoLyInfo/NIMS MatNavi and PI1M are both topically relevant (amine/diamine-bearing polymer precursors) but contractually blocked for bulk ingestion (MatNavi Terms of Use ban bulk acquisition; PI1M README states 'Data for academic purpose only'), and this fire could not independently re-fetch a byte-exact quote of the MatNavi terms page (relied on an indexed search snippet).
proposed_followups.proposed_done_criterion: A future fire (or a human) directly loads polymer.nims.go.jp's MatNavi Service Terms of Use page (post-login if required) and quotes the exact clause byte-for-byte, and separately obtains a written academic/commercial-use clarification from the PI1M authors before this cron treats either source as usable.

tanimoto_method.honest_caveat: This is NOT the same bit-width/convention as the AD gate's own pinned instrument (Morgan r=2/256-bit Tanimoto to nearest Bemis-Murcko scaffold representative, per U-AD sha256 3d229e2f016a22d23b27c2aef17adcbf5be80b760ecb11988c69a5155425eba3). It is used here only to establish EXACT-vs-not structural identity between a candidate dataset's named chemical and the 5-canonical-amine / grammar-38 SMILES already on file in-repo -- both fingerprints agree on Tanimoto=1.0 for an identical SMILES string regardless of bit-width/convention, so the exact-match findings below (DETA, MDA/DDM) are convention-independent.

why: The claim under attack ('rights-clean training corpora exist that would widen the AD') is SUPPORTED by concrete evidence: two independently-verified CC-BY-4.0 sources (Mendeley 10.17632/bypjxzm3fn.1, Zenodo 10.31142/ijtsrd15748) carry EXACT structural matches (Tanimoto=1.0000) to a currently-excluded canonical amine (DETA) and a currently-unrepresented grammar-38 novel candidate (MDA/DDM) respectively. However, the verdict is reported as BLOCKED_DATA rather than a bare affirmation because actually widening the AD requires a human/future-fire step this fire does not perform: downloading the licensed files, hand-verifying the property rows against the published source, and re-ingesting them into the training corpus with provenance -- i.e. forward motion on the underlying objective (a wider AD) is blocked on that acquisition step, even though the rights-clearance search itself succeeded. 15 of 17 swept sources were near-misses or blocked (chemotype mismatch, NC/SA licence conditions, unverifiable quotes, or explicit bulk-acquisition bans), each honestly recorded rather than silently dropped -- most notably, NIST ThermoML/TRC data was found to be Standard Reference Data (15 U.S.C. 290e carve-out), NOT covered by NIST's general public-domain policy as an earlier informal assumption might have implied, and is logged as BLOCKED_RIGHTS with a verbatim quote rather than assumed clean.
